title: Pointers, references, and callbacks

spans.text: A pointer stores an address and may be `nullptr`; a reference is another name for an existing object and must be initialized. A reference parameter avoids copying; `const T&` reads a large object without copying it. `T**` stores the address of a pointer. `void*` can hold an untyped address but must be converted to the correct type before use. A function pointer or callback passes an operation to run when an event occurs.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Pointer arithmetic is valid only within the same array; it is not defined for `void*`. Dereferencing a null, invalid, or expired address can corrupt or crash a program. Callback and ISR rules depend on the library and board; never call blocking code from an ISR.
